text.arabic_uthmani: وَمَا لِىَ لَآ أَعْبُدُ ٱلَّذِى فَطَرَنِى وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ

words.gloss_range: opening connector that resumes the prior exhortation and turns it into the speaker's own rationale
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) makes the ayah continue the live speech from 36:21 instead of opening a detached meditation. The same bound one-letter connector carries the prior command into a self-question, so the reader hears continuation before the question particle arrives. Its force can be heard as coordination and resumption together: one speech continues, but its mode changes from command to personal testimony.

topics.headline: continued speech after 36:21
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah continues the argument from 36:21 rather than beginning a separate topic.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence read the word as a clause-opening connector before the rhetorical question, keeping the self-question tied to the preceding exhortation.

topics.headline: command becomes testimony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the rhetorical move from telling others to follow into showing the speaker's own reason for worship.
topics.reason: The connector introduces the speaker's self-interrogation immediately after the prior imperative, so the register change is local and discourse-bound.

topics.headline: single-letter transition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that continuation and pivot are compressed into a bound one-letter opening before the question is heard.
topics.reason: The bound connector is the actual first surface element and can carry both connective and resumptive force without choosing only one.

words.gloss_range: rhetorical reason-seeking interrogative, with negative-litotes pressure that strengthens the affirmation
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) opens the self-question as a search for any possible warrant for non-worship. The local grammar primarily makes it interrogative, not a neutral request for information but a public self-test whose expected answer is that no such reason exists. The rest of the ayah then answers the question by identifying the worshipped through origination and expanding the answer to the audience's return. The possible negative reparse does not replace that reading; it reinforces the same result, turning question plus negation into emphatic affirmation. The open cadence across the question-negation sequence makes that logical frame audible before the worship verb arrives.

topics.headline: reason-seeking question
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the question asks what reason could justify non-worship, not what object is being sought.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as interrogative in the nominal question, and translation support marks the construction as rhetorical rather than information-seeking.

topics.headline: negative reparse strengthens affirmation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that an alternate negative segmentation would still converge on the same emphatic affirmation of worship.
topics.reason: The local QAC row selects interrogative force, so the negative reading is kept as reparse pressure rather than made the controlling parse.

topics.headline: question frames the sentence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rest of the ayah arrives as the answer to the compact opening question.
topics.reason: The one-word interrogative begins the nominal question, and the following identification and return clauses supply its rationale and expansion.

words.gloss_range: first-person dative of personal pertinence in the rhetorical question, carrying stake, reason, benefit, and duty pressure
words.prose: {{ar:لِىَ}} ({{tr:liya}}) makes the question personally indexed before the worship verb arrives. The phrase is the predicative complement of the opening question, so the issue is what could pertain to the speaker himself as a reason, benefit, or duty against worship. The first-person suffix contracts the public exhortation into testimony, while the later plural return will reopen the address to the audience. The shorter variant changes recitational weight at the self-anchor without changing that referent.

topics.headline: personal stake
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the question is first tested on the speaker's own stake before being pressed onto the audience.
topics.reason: The prefixed preposition with the first-person suffix is governed in the rhetorical question and refers to the speaker introduced in 36:20.

topics.headline: necessary question complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase is not ornamental; it supplies the predicate expression that lets the question mean what is there for me.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the phrase as the predicate expression of the interrogative construction.

topics.headline: reason, benefit, and duty pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the personal dative thickens the question beyond bare possession into what reason, benefit, or obligation could justify refusal.
topics.reason: The local construction licenses pertinence and personal stake; the broader benefit and duty shades are kept as pressure rather than separate meanings all equally selected.

topics.headline: public address contracts into me
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the pronoun movement from public address into the speaker's me before the ayah returns to you.
topics.reason: The first-person suffix belongs to the same speaker, while the final verb carries second-person plural agreement.

topics.headline: variant preserves self-reference
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the variant can tighten or lengthen the cadence at the self-anchor without changing the speaker reference.
topics.reason: The variant affects recitational shape, while the first-person governed pronoun relation remains the same.

words.gloss_range: negation of the ongoing first-person worship verb inside a rhetorical question, staging non-worship only to make it untenable
words.prose: {{ar:لَآ}} ({{tr:lā}}) places non-worship inside the question as the stance being tested. Its scope reaches the ongoing worship verb and its object, but it does not negate the following origination clause; the creative act remains the positive warrant inside the hypothetical refusal. Because the particle is negating rather than prohibitive, the verb stays a first-person indicative statement under scrutiny, and the long negation gives the rejected alternative audible weight before the worship verb overturns it.

topics.headline: negation scopes over worship
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the negation targets ongoing non-worship, while the origination clause remains positive evidence.
topics.reason: Translation support fixes the negation scope over the worship verb and object, not over the relative clause's creative act.

topics.headline: non-worship made untenable
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that non-worship is voiced only as the alternative the question exposes as irrational.
topics.reason: The rhetorical question frame makes the negated clause function as affirmation by asking what could justify the negative alternative.

topics.headline: negating, not prohibiting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle modifies the speaker's statement without turning the verb into a command.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the word as a negative particle before the indicative imperfect verb, not as a prohibitive command particle.

words.gloss_range: first-person imperfect active worship, service, devotion, and obedience directed to a definite object identified by origination
words.root_gloss_range: worship, service, obedience, devotion, subjection, and related smoothing or making-passable imagery; the local Form I verb selects the speaker's own worshipful service, not causative subjugation
words.prose: {{ar:أَعْبُدُ}} ({{tr:aʿbudu}}) is the speaker's ongoing active worship in the middle of a question that rejects non-worship. The verb carries its first-person subject internally and takes a direct relative-pronoun object, so devotion is not left abstract; it is aimed at {{ar:ٱلَّذِى فَطَرَنِى}} ({{tr:alladhī faṭaranī}}), the one who originated the speaker. The root range gives worship the texture of service, obedience, and submitted allegiance, and its road-smoothing image makes submission feel like making one's course passable toward the originator; the local Form I active still keeps the action as the speaker's own worship rather than causative subjugation or literal road-making. Its imperfect form and public utterance make the claim a present stance, with the sharp onset landing after the long negation and the sound flowing directly into the relative object. The singular {{ar:أَعْبُدُ}} ({{tr:aʿbudu}}) also stands near broader imperfect worship formulas such as 1:5 and 109, while remaining the lone speaker's testimony; its active voice contrasts with the audience being returned passively at the close.

topics.headline: worship aimed at identified object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that worship is grammatically aimed at the one defined by origination, not left as a general religious action.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the relative pronoun as the explicit direct object of the worship verb.

topics.headline: ongoing speaker-owned worship
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices worship as the speaker's present continuing stance, carried inside the verb rather than by a separate pronoun.
topics.reason: The local form is first-person singular imperfect active, and contextual profiles show this root-form strongly supports explicit-object worship frames.

topics.headline: statement under negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word remains a first-person indicative statement under negation, not a command not to worship.
topics.reason: The preceding particle is a negator of the imperfect verb, not a prohibitive particle changing the verb into a command.

topics.headline: worship as submitted allegiance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the worship word carries devotion, service, obedience, and allegiance rather than bare acknowledgement.
topics.reason: The lexical range fits the local active worship frame and the speech act publicly performs the allegiance it names.

topics.headline: submitted path image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a concrete submitted-path image in the root family, while the local verb still means the speaker worships and serves.
topics.reason: The road-smoothing image belongs to related root-family evidence, but the local Form I direct-object worship frame selects worshipful service rather than literal paving or making another subservient.

topics.headline: Form I active limits causative force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the contrast between chosen active worship now and passive return later, with causative subjugation kept outside the local form.
topics.reason: The aligned verb is active Form I first-person worship, while the final return verb is passive; no local Form II causative frame is present.

topics.headline: worship linked to origin and return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that worship is framed between the one who originated the speaker and the endpoint to whom the audience is returned.
topics.reason: The local sequence gives the worship verb a direct relative object completed by origination and followed by the return clause.

topics.headline: singular worship in formulaic register
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a lone speaker's {{ar:أَعْبُدُ}} ({{tr:aʿbudu}}) stands near broader imperfect worship formulas such as 1:5 and 109, while remaining singular and locally grounded in his own origination.
topics.reason: The recurrence rows name concrete worship-register parallels, but local morphology keeps this occurrence first-person singular rather than communal.

topics.headline: sound lands the worship claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sharp onset and flow into the relative object as an audible landing of the central worship claim.
topics.reason: The sound observations are local to the actual surface sequence and reinforce, without changing, the grammar of the worship claim.

words.gloss_range: definite masculine singular relative pronoun that identifies the worshipped referent through the following origination clause
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِى}} ({{tr:alladhī}}) prevents the object of worship from being generic by making it a definite relative referent. Instead of naming a title, the pronoun points forward to {{ar:فَطَرَنِى}} ({{tr:faṭaranī}}), so the act of origination does the identifying work. Its position bridges worship to creation, and the later suffix in {{ar:إِلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ilayhi}}) resumes the same referent as the destination of return.

topics.headline: identity through action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the worshipped one is identified by the act of originating the speaker, not by a separate title.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun introduces the relative clause whose verb identifies the referent as the one who originated the speaker.

topics.headline: direct object of worship
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the pronoun as the hinge where worship moves directly into its reason.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the pronoun as the direct object of the worship verb and the subject of the origination verb.

topics.headline: same referent reaches return clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the originator named by the relative clause is also the one to whom the audience is returned.
topics.reason: Cross-reference evidence links the later third-person suffix back to the referent established by the relative pronoun and its clause.

topics.headline: compressed relative linkage
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one relative pronoun both makes the referent definite and pulls the sentence forward to the defining action.
topics.reason: The fixed relative-pronoun form combines definiteness with linkage and remains incomplete until the following verb supplies its predicate.

words.gloss_range: completed active origination of the speaker, with the first-person object suffix making the creative act personally indexed
words.root_gloss_range: origination, creating, cleaving or opening, formation, and created disposition; the local perfect transitive verb selects personal origination while preserving cleaving and disposition pressure as image and undertone
words.prose: {{ar:فَطَرَنِى}} ({{tr:faṭaranī}}) supplies the defining action promised by {{ar:ٱلَّذِى}} ({{tr:alladhī}}): the worshipped one is the one who originated the speaker. The perfect active form makes origination a completed act with the originator's agency visible, while the attached first-person suffix makes the speaker the affected object. The root's cleaving and formation images sharpen origination as emergence into being, with the emphatic central release matching that rupture texture, and the created-disposition field keeps it from sounding like neutral manufacture; locally, however, the selected sense remains personal origination. The same personal origination wording joins individual testimony in 11:51 and 43:27. That completed origin becomes the reason for the ongoing worship and the first pole of the origin-return arc.

topics.headline: completed origination of me
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the warrant for worship is a completed origination personally attached to the speaker.
topics.reason: The verb is a perfect active form with a first-person object suffix, and attachment evidence marks that suffix as the direct object.

topics.headline: originator agency stays visible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices both sides of the relation: the originator acts and the speaker receives the act.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun is the subject of the active verb, and the attached first-person suffix is its object.

topics.headline: definition completes the relative pronoun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sentence identifies the worshipped one through this single originating act.
topics.reason: The verb is the predicate of the relative clause and completes the identification opened by the preceding relative pronoun.

topics.headline: cleaving into being
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices origination with a concrete cleaving and formation texture, while the local verb still means the speaker was originated.
topics.reason: Dictionary-root evidence supports cleaving and formation imagery, but the local human object and relative clause select personal origination rather than a literal physical split or dough-working event.

topics.headline: created disposition undertone
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that origination implies a made constitution or disposition, while the local word remains a verb of originating the speaker.
topics.reason: The root's disposition field is relevant as undertone, but the local surface is the perfect verb with the first-person object, not the abstract noun in 30:30.

topics.headline: personal origination formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this personal origination wording joins similar individual testimony in 11:51 and 43:27.
topics.reason: The rows provide concrete recurrence references, and the local wording shares the personal origination form without needing to name the speaker by title.

topics.headline: origin grounds worship and return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices origination as the ayah's central engine: it explains worship and sets up the return clause.
topics.reason: The local clause sequence joins worship, origination, and return, and the contextual profile marks this form as a comparatively limited, salient origination form.

words.gloss_range: connector opening the return clause, joining origination to return while allowing coordination, circumstantial, or resumptive force
words.prose: The second {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the hinge between the speaker's personal origination and the audience's return. It can be heard as simple coordination, circumstantial while-force, or resumption into a fresh assertion, but all of those readings keep the return clause bound to what precedes. By fusing with the destination phrase, it introduces a new clause whose first audible content is the destination, with that onset giving the linked clause a fresh acoustic entry. It makes the shift from me to you a controlled pivot rather than a detached add-on.

topics.headline: origin joined to return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that origination and return are joined as two parts of one divine relation without collapsing into one clause.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats the return clause as coordinated after the origination clause.

topics.headline: while and resumption remain live
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the connector can make return either the surrounding circumstance of worship or a fresh assertion after the origin claim.
topics.reason: The local syntax strongly licenses a new coordinated clause, so circumstantial and resumptive readings are preserved as layered force rather than mutually exclusive parses.

topics.headline: new clause before destination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the connector launches a clause whose first content is the fronted destination phrase, not a stray attachment to the previous verb.
topics.reason: The return clause begins with the connector plus fronted prepositional phrase and is syntactically tied to the passive return verb.

topics.headline: me-to-you pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the exact hinge where first-person testimony turns back toward the second-person audience.
topics.reason: The connector follows the first-person object in the origination verb and precedes the second-person plural passive return verb.

words.gloss_range: fronted goal-direction phrase with a third-person suffix, marking the definite personal endpoint of the return
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ilayhi}}) places the destination before the return verb. The preposition marks endpoint, and the suffix makes that endpoint personal and already known: the same referent identified as {{ar:ٱلَّذِى فَطَرَنِى}} ({{tr:alladhī faṭaranī}}). Because the phrase stays syntactically dependent on {{ar:تُرْجَعُونَ}} ({{tr:turjaʿūna}}), its fronting does not detach it; it foregrounds where the audience is returned before the passive action is heard. The result is a relational terminus, not a vague place or route, and the long-vowel movement from {{ar:إِلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ilayhi}}) into {{ar:تُرْجَعُونَ}} ({{tr:turjaʿūna}}) helps the final return clause feel like a landing.

topics.headline: personal endpoint of return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the return is to the identified originator, not to an unspecified place.
topics.reason: Cross-reference evidence routes the suffix back to the referent identified by the relative clause, and the preposition marks the destination of the passive return.

topics.headline: destination before action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the destination before hearing the action of being returned, giving the endpoint strong focus.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence keeps the fronted phrase dependent on the return verb, while word order places it before the verb.

topics.headline: endpoint, not route
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause is about final destination rather than the route, means, or cause of return.
topics.reason: The preposition is locally the goal-direction complement of the passive return verb.

topics.headline: compressed destination phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that direction and referent are fused in one compact phrase whose sound carries the clause toward closure.
topics.reason: The preposition plus suffix compresses endpoint and referent, and the sound note is local to the actual final phrase.

words.gloss_range: second-person plural imperfect passive return directed to the fronted personal endpoint, presenting the audience as those being returned
words.root_gloss_range: returning, reverting, recurrence, echo, and returning rain imagery; local passive imperfect with a goal phrase selects being returned to the identified originator while preserving cyclical and reverberating pressure as image
words.prose: {{ar:تُرْجَعُونَ}} ({{tr:turjaʿūna}}) closes the ayah by turning the speaker's self-reasoning back onto the audience. The second-person plural ending embeds you inside the final verb, while the passive form makes the addressees patients of return rather than agents who return themselves. Its imperfect aspect leaves the return impending or ongoing, and the fronted {{ar:إِلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ilayhi}}) supplies the destination before the action arrives. The root's echo, recurrence, and returning-rain images can color the return as movement back to source, but the local frame selects passive return to the identified originator. The active variant reading exposes the agency fork without replacing the canonical passive, and the u-vowel passive opening makes that agency difference audible. The same return language anticipates the surah's closing formula at 36:83, with the final -ūna ending reinforcing the semantic closure, and binds worship, origination, and return into one compressed human arc.

topics.headline: audience embedded in final verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final turn from the speaker's me to the audience's you inside the verb morphology.
topics.reason: The verb carries second-person plural agreement, while the prior origination clause carried the first-person object suffix.

topics.headline: being returned, not self-return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the audience does not grammatically control the return; they are made the affected party of it.
topics.reason: The local verb is passive with no expressed agent and a second-person plural patient agreement.

topics.headline: imperfect return remains open
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the return as impending or continuing rather than a completed past event.
topics.reason: The aligned form is an imperfect passive, not a completed passive alternative.

topics.headline: return needs its endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that passive return is not directionless; the fronted phrase supplies the endpoint before the verb arrives.
topics.reason: The valency profile and attachment evidence show this passive return form regularly takes a goal complement, and locally the fronted phrase supplies it.

topics.headline: echo and recurrence back to source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the return as movement back to source with echo, recurrence, and returning-rain texture, while the local verb remains passive return to Him.
topics.reason: The root-family images are relevant as pressure, but the local construction with a goal phrase selects being returned to the identified referent rather than independent rain or sound meanings.

topics.headline: passive form contrasted with active variant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the canonical passive foregrounds removed human agency, while the active variant exposes the agency contrast without replacing the local form.
topics.reason: The canonical surface is passive, and the variant is useful as contrast but does not control the local parse.

topics.headline: worship, origin, return sequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a compressed arc in which worship stands between created origin and inevitable return.
topics.reason: The local sentence explicitly contains the worship, origination, and return roots in sequence, with the return clause closing the argument.

topics.headline: surah-level return anticipation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the man's closing phrase anticipates the return formula that closes the surah at 36:83 and resonates with return language at 36:50 and 36:67.
topics.reason: The rows provide concrete same-surah references, including the exact closing formula at 36:83.

topics.headline: final-word expansion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the last word expands the argument from private testimony to public consequence and prepares the next ayah's alternative-gods question.
topics.reason: The final verb closes the current ayah and is followed in 36:23 by the question about taking gods besides Him.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The active first-person worship verb stands between the one who originated the speaker and the passive plural return to Him.
baseline_models.mechanism: Origination establishes an asymmetric prior claim, worship is the speaker's active answer to that claim, and compulsory return closes the trajectory for speaker and audience.

activation_trace.role: Humble obedient service supplies the voluntary response at the center of the trajectory.
First origination supplies the prior act that makes the speaker's service intelligible.
Being sent back toward a prior source closes the arc and extends its consequence to the audience.

changed_reading.before: The speaker simply says that a creator deserves worship and everyone will return.
changed_reading.after: The ayah forms an origin-service-return trajectory: received existence calls for active service before an unavoidable return.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The opening sense of the origination root, the prepared-way range of the worship root, and the motion range of return can be read together.
baseline_models.mechanism: The one who opened the speaker into existence also makes a traversable course; worship is enacted passage on that course, and return names its destination.

activation_trace.role: Splitting something open supplies the image of existence as an opened passage.
Making a way level and usable turns worship into the act of taking a prepared course.
Ordered steps and changes of gait provide the route's directed movement back.

changed_reading.before: Worship is a static duty owed to a maker.
changed_reading.after: Worship can also be carried as traversal of the very way opened by the originator toward return.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction begins with the speaker questioning his own non-worship, names what was done to him, and ends by addressing the audience's return.
baseline_models.mechanism: The first-person self-question prevents detached exhortation: the speaker makes his own service evidence before transferring the consequence of return to the plural audience.

activation_trace.role: Personal obedient service gives the speaker a practice with which to address others.
The speaker's own origination makes the argument self-implicating rather than abstract.
The speech-response range supports the rhetorical handoff from the speaker's case to his addressees.

changed_reading.before: The line is an impersonal proposition about proper worship.
changed_reading.after: The speaker argues through enacted witness: his own response to being originated becomes a question placed before those who will return.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding runner performs purposeful movement and urges pursuit of guides who demand no compensation; the focus speaker's worship therefore functions as embodied, nontransactional path testimony.

activation_trace.role: Personal obedient service is the practice whose credibility the preceding movement tests.
Purposeful motion toward an objective makes the man's counsel visibly enacted.
Following behind supplies the directional relation that the focus service continues.
Work-compensation language marks the guides' refusal to make this path a transaction.
Gentle direction toward the right way identifies the path the speaker is modeling.

structural_cues: The focus ayah directly follows two imperatives to follow and retains the same first-person speaker.
The speaker moves from addressing his people to interrogating his own conduct.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies purposeful movement, following, lack of requested payment, and guidance; I infer that the speaker's worship demonstrates the recommended path; alternatively, the focus may be only a separate argument after the call to follow.

changed_reading.before: The speaker's self-question is a private confession of creator-directed worship.
changed_reading.after: His self-question is public path evidence: he runs, follows nontransactional guidance, and embodies the service he recommends.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayat test alternative objects of service as protective intermediaries: they remain short of the ultimate source, cannot join the speaker effectively in intercession, and cannot extract him from harm.

activation_trace.role: Obedient service becomes the disputed allocation of dependence.
The final return sets the horizon within which a claimed protector must prove effective.
Nearness that falls short of the goal locates substitute objects below the ultimate relation.
An object receiving worship makes the alternative dependency explicit.
A would-be advocate joining another party supplies the proposed mediation mechanism.
Extraction from another's grip supplies the rescue test that the alternatives fail.
Missing the intended way names the result of assigning service to failed protectors.

structural_cues: The speaker continues in the first person immediately after the focus.
The counterfactual harm-rescue sequence tests the practical consequence of taking alternatives.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies alternative worship, proposed mediation, failed extraction, and lost direction; I infer that reliable dependence is a criterion for worship; alternatively, these ayat may only refute other gods without defining the positive service relation.

changed_reading.before: Worship is owed because the speaker was created.
changed_reading.after: Worship also allocates ultimate dependence: only the origin and destination relation survives the test of harm, mediation, and rescue.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah contrasts the dead's inability to return to their people with every dispersed person being gathered and made present; the focus return is therefore a terminal transfer of venue, not restoration of ordinary social access.

activation_trace.role: Return toward a prior source supplies the focus destination whose character the context specifies.
Denied return to earlier people blocks an ordinary homeward reading.
Recombining what was dispersed makes the return comprehensive and collective.
Compelled proximity and witnessed presence specify the destination of gathering.
The inability to get back to family removes the final familiar return route.
A second total gathering confirms that no dispersed member remains outside.
A second compelled presence fixes the return as appearance before the divine speaker.

structural_cues: Two non-return statements concern predecessors or family, while two matching formulas place everyone before God.
The passive force of the focus return aligns with the later passive presentation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies blocked human return and total divine gathering; I infer a transfer from inaccessible human relations into compulsory divine presence; alternatively, the gathering formulas may state only universality rather than redefine return.

changed_reading.before: Return is a general homecoming to the creator.
changed_reading.after: Return is irreversible collective presentation: death closes routes back to people while opening unavoidable presence before God.

context_deltas.mechanism: Dead ground becomes living, concealed grain emerges, water bursts through, and daylight is peeled away; these transformations sharpen origination as productive opening and exposure rather than static manufacture.

activation_trace.role: Opening by rupture supplies the focus image that the later transformations amplify.

structural_cues: The sign sequence repeatedly moves from closed, dead, or covered states to exposed life, food, water, or darkness.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies several opening-like transformations; I infer that they materially exemplify the focus origination root; alternatively, they may be independent signs of power rather than specifications of that root.

changed_reading.before: The originator performed a one-time act of making the speaker.
changed_reading.after: The originator is recognized through recurrent productive openings that expose life and provision from sealed or contrary states.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later address recasts worship as a preserved covenant with two opposed allegiances: service to a severing enemy or service to God as the straight route.

activation_trace.role: The speaker's obedient service supplies the allegiance later made explicit.

The repeated service root shows that obedience can be allocated to the wrong claimant.
Distance and severance make the rival service a route away from the origin relation.
Open hostility identifies the rival allegiance as actively opposed to its servants.
The positive imperative confirms God-directed service as the covenant's required allegiance.
A direct, upright road turns allegiance into the route governing conduct and destination.

structural_cues: The later address repeats the focus worship root in a prohibition and an imperative.
The imperative is immediately identified with a straight path.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies covenant, opposed service, an enemy, and a straight path; I infer that worship establishes route allegiance; alternatively, the path may describe the consequence of worship rather than its mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The speaker worships because creation creates an individual obligation.
changed_reading.after: His worship enacts a preserved communal covenant and chooses the straight allegiance over service that severs creatures from their source.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing sequence makes first origination evidence for reviving decomposed bodies, then adds effective command, comprehensive sovereignty, and an exact return echo; origin is thus both warrant and capacity for return.

activation_trace.role: The speaker's origination supplies the first endpoint later used as evidence.
The audience's return supplies the second endpoint whose mechanism the close unfolds.
Human creation from a minute beginning restates origination at bodily scale.
Bringing a thing newly into existence supplies the precedent for bodily revival.
Priority and first beginning identify the earlier creation as the relevant precedent.
Repeated creative bringing-forth expands the precedent from one human to cosmic scale.
An effective directive supplies the operative transition from intention to renewed existence.
Comprehensive sovereignty supplies jurisdiction over every being that returns.
The closing repetition of return seals the focus trajectory at surah scale.

structural_cues: The answer to who revives bones explicitly appeals to their first origination.
The final ayah repeats the focus return construction after command and sovereignty.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies first origination, renewed creation, effective command, sovereignty, and repeated return; I infer that origination is the evidentiary and causal bridge to return; alternatively, the close may prove resurrection without making it the focus ayah's internal mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Creation and return are two asserted endpoints supporting worship.
changed_reading.after: The first endpoint executes the second: initial origination demonstrates and grounds the power to re-originate every creature into final return.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it reads celestial recurrence into a personal eschatological return. It remains anchored in the focus return root and in the surah's measured running, returning phase, and circular course. Render it only as a structural echo of ordered motion, not as a claim that final return is merely a natural cycle.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The passive plural return can be heard against the surah's repeated created motions toward stations and back through measured phases.

activation_trace.role: Movement back toward a source supplies the personal return that the cosmic pattern echoes.
Continuous running supplies directed created motion toward an appointed station.
Deliberate measure and ordering make the motion governed rather than accidental.
Coming back after departure supplies an explicit recurrent counterpart to return.
Rounded circulation places each moving body within a bounded created course.

changed_reading.before: Return is an isolated future transport with no visible analogue.
changed_reading.after: Return gains a restrained cosmic analogue: created beings move within measured courses whose destinations and recurrences are already governed.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it reads the later livestock economy back through the service root. It remains anchored because the focus inventory spans owned servitude, imposed subduing, prepared usability, and honoring, while the context places human ownership and taming beneath divine creation. Render it as an inversion that distinguishes willing honor from animal domestication, not as a claim that worship lexically means livestock management.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The first-person service verb carries both coercive and honoring branch possibilities, while its rhetorical form presents a reasoned personal response.

activation_trace.role: Owned servitude supplies the coercive pole against which the speaker's self-address can be tested.
Honor and magnification supply a noncoercive pole for the same service root.
Divine bringing-forth places the human ownership scene inside a prior creative relation.
Human possession and disposal rights supply the lower-level master-creature relation.
Making a difficult creature tractable and usable supplies the explicit domestication mechanism.
Recognition of benefit redirects human mastery toward acknowledgment of the higher giver.

changed_reading.before: Worship is imagined primarily as the creator's imposed mastery over a servant.
changed_reading.after: The later ownership scene invites an inversion: humans tame owned creatures, but their own creator-directed service is voiced as self-chosen honor and grateful recognition.

strongest_changes: First origination becomes the evidentiary and operative bridge to bodily return.
Worship becomes covenantal route allegiance, opposed both to a severing enemy and to failed substitute rescuers.
Return is sharpened into irreversible collective presentation rather than restoration to family or predecessors.
The opening range of origination is activated by dead land, emergence, burst water, and peeled-away light.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah context makes the speaker's self-question a hinge between embodied guidance and failed protection, then replays its service, origination, and return roots through covenant, creaturely economy, resurrection, and the closing return.
remaining_uncertainties: The ecological opening model may be analogical rather than a deliberate specification of the origination root.
The measured-orbit model should remain a structural echo because terminal return need not be cyclical.
The ownership and taming inversion is branch-driven and should not displace the ordinary obedient-service sense.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Worship answers origination with return.** `ع ب د` B003 is worshipful submission, `ف ط ر` B001 opening/splitting and B002 initiating existence, and `ر ج ع` B001 return. The first-person origin is paired with the audience's second-person return, producing a shared trajectory despite the pronoun shift. I infer that the originator's claim persists through the creature's entire arc. Worship reads as alignment of beginning and destination.
2. **Creation opens what return closes.** `ف ط ر` B001 supplies splitting open, while `ر ج ع` B001 reverses movement. Later the graves open into swift movement (36:51) and worn bones are revived (36:78-79). I infer a reversible material logic: the one who first opens existence can reopen its closed state. The ayah quietly carries resurrection force before the explicit challenge.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 36:51's grave-exit and 36:79's appeal to first origination made the opening/return structure materially explicit: return is a reopening by the same originating agency.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Worship spans the arc from opening into existence to return.** **ع ب د B003** anchors submissive worship in **أَعْبُدُ**; **ف ط ر B001** supplies opening/splitting and **ف ط ر B002** initiation in **فَطَرَنِى**; **ر ج ع B001** anchors return. The fixed switch from first-person creation to second-person return is supplied, as are guidance immediately before (36:21) and failed alternative gods immediately after (36:23). The inferred arrow is *the source that opens a life into being also determines its terminal direction, making worship the fitting alignment of the interval*. The question becomes trajectory-based reasoning rather than isolated devotion.
2. **The singular source gathers a dispersed people back.** **ر ج ع B001** includes causing others to return, while the address shifts to plural **تُرْجَعُونَ**. The man addresses his people in 36:20, and 36:26–27 later wishes that same people could know his transformed state. The packet supplies his singular testimony and corporate concern; the abduction is *personal recognition is used as a pivot intended to turn the collective*. Return is therefore already socially active in the speech.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: **Later surprise.** The passive entry of 36:26 and the forgiveness/honor of 36:27 give “return” a protected arrival-state. The origin-to-return arc in 36:22 therefore closes not merely in movement back but in reassignment by the originator.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi hem bir şeyin kendiliğinden önceki yerine veya durumuna dönmesini hem de bir başkasının onu geri göndermesini aynı çekirdekte toplar. Tekrarlama da bu geri dönüş düzeninin bir uzantısıdır.

Bir kişi veya etken, başka bir şeyi önceki yerine ya da ilgililerine geri gönderir.
Geri dönüş düzeni, bir eylemin yeniden yapılması anlamına genişleyebilir.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Nihai yöneliş, yeniden diriltilme ve dünyaya yeniden gelme ayrı bağlamsal gerçekleşmelerdir; sıradan mekansal dönüş bu dala girmez.

Belirli bir inanç kullanımında ölümden sonra yeniden dünyaya gelme de dönüş adıyla anılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi aynı adı yağmur, yeniden gelen su, su birikintisi ve vadilerin su toplayan üst kesimleri için verir. Tekrarlanan su hareketi ortak bağdır, fakat bu yer ve su türleri eş anlamlı değildir.

Suyun henüz toplanmadan önce yöneldiği vadi üstleri çoğul bir biçimle adlandırılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kanıt yağmuru temel görünüm olarak paylaşır; su birikintisi, titreşen su ve vadi üstleri aynı geri gelen su tasarımının yer ve sonuç uzantılarıdır.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Satıştan sonra bedelle yerine mal alma, tahsilde karşılık kabul etme ve yeniden satış değeri ayrı ekonomik ilişkilerdir; satışın geri alınmasıyla karıştırılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir süreçten geçtikten sonra geri çıkan, yeniden getirilen veya ikinci kez işlenen şeydir. Sindirimden dönen geviş ve dışkı bunun bedensel görünümleri; yeniden ısıtılan yemek, sökülüp yapılan giysi ve sahibine geri çevrilen söz ise yapıya bağlı görünümleridir.

facets.statement: Bir madde veya ürün önceki işlemden sonra geri gelir ya da yeniden işlenir.
Hayvanın yeniden çiğnemek için ağzına getirdiği geviş ile sindirimden çıkan dışkı, geri dönen madde olarak adlandırılır.
Soğuduktan sonra yeniden ısıtılan yemek ile sökülüp yeniden yapılan veya eskimiş giysi, ikinci kez işlenmiş ürünlerdir.
Sahibine geri çevrilen veya yinelenen söz, aynı geri gönderme şemasının iletişimsel kullanımıdır.
